summary: Mount Baker lookout near Cranbrook, BC: a 1913 Forest Branch station, watchmen in 1921 and 1932, a 1964 plan for a new tower, and a 2026 listing as standing.

facts.status_note: A 2026 guide lists it among lookouts confirmed or likely to have standing structures; no inspection is cited.

staffing.status: No current staffing found; last record is a 1932 City of Cranbrook lookout man

events.note: Provincial Forest Branch built a lookout station and cabin on the summit, with six miles of trail and six miles of telephone line.
Canadian Forestry Journal item says a lookout would be stationed at the point through the fire season.
Tom Dalton was in charge of the fire lookout station on Mount Baker (Creston Review).
City of Cranbrook had a lookout man posted on top of the mountain to report fires near the municipal watershed.

B.C. Forest Service announced plans for a new fire tower at 7,000 ft above sea level, to be a primary lookout. The plan was for a prefabricated frame building, with the site to be the key radio repeater for East Kootenay ranger stations. Completion is not confirmed in the sources found.
Rainlander guide lists the Baker Fire Lookout (Cranbrook) among BC lookouts confirmed or likely to have standing structures.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources differ: 7,100 ft (1913 Forest Branch annual report), 7,200 ft (1913 Canadian Forestry Journal item), 7,000 ft (1964 plan), and 2133 m (Canada Lookouts coordinates block, about 7,000 ft). The story gives the 1964 plan figure and says it is a plan.
Sources use Mount Baker and Baker Mountain for the same summit, and the 1913 reports use both. The story uses both names.

notes_for_editor: Brief's kind 'three_story' and access 'unknown' are not confirmed by any fetched page, so neither is recorded. Brief coordinates (49.45876, -115.6304) differ from the Canada Lookouts block (49.448, -115.612) by about 1.6 km; the story does not give coordinates. The Canada Lookouts page header says 'Cariboo' above content that is about East Kootenay; treat that label as an error on that page. No source confirms the 1964 tower was finished or whether the 1913 station was removed. A YouTube video and a Facebook thread mention comms equipment and an older tower on the summit; neither could be read. Waymarking rendered only its title. No photos recorded.
